summary: Interleaved sparse/dense embedding payloads from proxy causing partial rerank empty-sets and p95 latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer QueryFlow reports intermittent empty result sets from reranking endpoint accompanied by p95 token latency spikes. Impact: Several production queries for rerank returned empty candidate lists or truncated partial responses; user-visible degradation for a portion of traffic. Environment: Dedicated tenant in us-east using dedicated routing through the new proxy compaction feature rolled last week.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use QueryFlow test workload: 500 parallel rerank requests (batch size 32) to /v1/rerank with embedding payloads assembled by in-house proxy compaction. 2) Observe ~3-7% requests returning empty candidates or single-candidate responses. 3) Re-run with proxy compaction disabled -> behavior stops. 4) Run with canonical client sending explicit embedding-format header -> mitigates failures.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:22:11Z ERROR reranker: received embedding payloads count mismatch (expected 32 actual 28)
2026-03-10T14:22:11Z WARN proxy: compacted-segments reordered; missing segment-metadata header for request id=cf-7e3b
2026-03-10T14:22:12Z ERROR serving-runtime: fallback to CPU-ann due to ann-shard-miss; p95 latency 1240ms (baseline 210ms)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: payload compaction introduced by proxy optimization occasionally interleaves sparse (sparse-indexed) and dense embeddings without annotating per-segment encoding. The reranker expects consistent orientation per request. Reproduced locally by toggling proxy compaction flags: when compaction reorders segments and drops per-segment 'emb-format' metadata, the reranker sees mixed dtype/orientation and either filters out candidates or triggers a CPU fallback path causing high latency. Observed correlation with proxy release v1.14.2 and with multi-model routing where text-embedding-legacy-v1 coexists on same route. Confirmed presence of requests where Content-Length matched combined segments but segment-header-count was lower than actual segments (off by 1-5).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Customer noticed issue after proxy compaction feature was enabled for dedicated customers; provided traffic dump and headers.
Jonah Park (SRE): Reproduced in staging by enabling proxy compaction; tracked to proxy PR that changes segment packing logic. Opening INT follow-up to patch header validation.
Eng lead (Marta Li): Adding a defensive check in reranker to validate per-request segment headers and reject mixed-format payloads with a descriptive 422 so we can avoid silent empty-sets.
Customer (QueryFlow - Tom Nguyen): We saw this as intermittent failures across our night jobs; major impact to nightly syncs. Thanks for quick triage.
Jonah Park: Canary rollback of proxy compaction in us-east started 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC; monitoring for error-rate decrease.
Marta Li: PR created to add header validation and a metrics counter for mixed-format events: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/215
temporary_workaround: Disable proxy compaction for the affected tenant or set 'embed-format: explicit' header at the client to force per-segment annotations. Canary rollback applied to us-east; customer confirmed reduced failures.
next_steps: 1) Merge reranker validation PR and add a 422 response path for mixed-format payloads (PR #215). 2) Harden proxy compaction to always emit per-segment metadata; add integration tests that simulate interleaving. 3) Create an alert (SLO) on mixed-format counter and empty-rerank responses. 4) Run a rollback incidence review with proxy team and schedule full rollout after tests.
resolution: Partial mitigation: Canary rollback of proxy compaction removed majority of incidents in us-east. Patch PRs opened for both proxy and reranker; full fix scheduled for 2026-03-16 release. Assigned INT-4521 to proxy team for backfill integration tests and a follow-up postmortem.
